versioning: minor release: new scheduling inputs (L3 domains, sibling and reserved-core lending, -t auto) and schema 10

database_schema.change: columns l3_domains, split_domains, cpu_utilization added; no existing column of any row changes; rollback sets the schema back to 9 in place

node_config: config/zenobia-16core-node.json: the live 16-core node.json (0.7.2) plus topology, borrow.lend_reserved true, borrow.lend_siblings false, cpus "auto", smt_siblings from sysfs
features: L3-domain placement from sysfs: a job stays inside one domain when it fits; heavy jobs (half a domain or more) go to the emptiest domain, light jobs pack into the fullest that fits; --l3-domains N, --split-domains A,B; SIMQ_L3_DOMAINS, SIMQ_L3_DOMAIN_IDS, SIMQ_NUMA_NODES

SMT siblings can be lent to borrow jobs (borrow.lend_siblings) unless the owner runs with --exclusive-timing; off in the 16-core config (a busy sibling slowed an integer-heavy owner by 47%, SCHED_IDLE does not help)
borrow jobs on cores reserved for a waiting head job (borrow.lend_reserved), preempted by their policy when it starts
-t auto: 1.5 x p95 runtime of the last 20 succeeded runs of the name (family), rounded up to 5 min, at least 10 min
partition cpus "auto" (every physical core from sysfs); smt_siblings from sysfs
CPU utilization per finished job (schema 10), simq list USE column, simq show UNDER-USED, node utilization in simq partitions
admission ceiling published by the worker (admission.json) and shown by simq partitions
warning for owner jobs below priority 10 asking for 75%+ of the pool; head-of-queue wait in its reason
